events.name: Indiana Pacers at Oklahoma City Thunder

headlines.description: — Tyrese Haliburton and the never-say-die Indiana Pacers pulled off yet another last-second comeback, this time on the NBA's biggest stage.
headlines.shortLinkText: NBA Finals: Haliburton caps huge rally with winning jumper as Pacers stun Thunder 111-110 in Game 1

events.name: Indiana Pacers at Oklahoma City Thunder

headlines.description: — This has been Oklahoma City's formula all season: Lose one game, respond in the next.
headlines.shortLinkText: Game 2: Thunder open another big lead and keep control, topping Pacers 123-107 to even NBA Finals

events.name: Oklahoma City Thunder at Indiana Pacers

headlines.description: — Every time Indiana has lost a game in the last three months, it simply has come back to win the next one.
headlines.shortLinkText: Game 3: Pacers rally in the 4th, beat Thunder 116-107 to take 2-1 lead in NBA Finals

events.name: Oklahoma City Thunder at Indiana Pacers

headlines.description: — Game on the line, season quite possibly on the line, the Oklahoma City Thunder had only one place to turn.
headlines.shortLinkText: Game 4: Gilgeous-Alexander goes wild in the 4th, Thunder rally to top Pacers 111-104 and tie Finals

events.name: Indiana Pacers at Oklahoma City Thunder

headlines.description: — Game 5 was starting to look like Game 1 all over again. Oklahoma City, at home, takes a huge lead. Indiana comes roaring back in the fourth quarter.
headlines.shortLinkText: Game 5: Williams scores 40 points and Thunder win 120-109 for a 3-2 NBA Finals lead over Pacers

events.name: Oklahoma City Thunder at Indiana Pacers

headlines.description: — Season on the line, the Indiana Pacers did what they’ve done time and time again. They bucked the odds.
headlines.shortLinkText: Pacers roll past Thunder 108-91 to send the NBA Finals to a deciding Game 7

events.name: Indiana Pacers at Oklahoma City Thunder

headlines.description: — Shai Gilgeous-Alexander walked off the court for the final time this season, collapsed into the arms of coach Mark Daigneault and finally smiled.
headlines.shortLinkText: Game 7: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scores 29 points and Thunder beat Pacers 103-91 for NBA title
